items.item: Abstract byte state (init/uninit, provenance fragment)

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:12,29 (typed copies reset padding to uninit; UCG#301, UCG#558)

items.disagreements: FLS (fls_6lg0oaaopc26) treats uninitialized memory only at value creation rather than defining per-byte provenance fragments; Reference (r[undefined.validity.const-provenance]), UCG, and MiniRust explicitly model 256 init values plus Uninit and provenance per byte.
items.rustc_deviations: In runtime LLVM codegen, uninitialized bytes lower to LLVM poison/undef; LLVM's byte-level poison propagation across bitwise/integer operations has historical edge cases (rust-lang/rust#71043) where Miri/MiniRust strictly track per-byte Uninit.

items.item: Data race is immediate UB; C++20 access-based atomic ordering model (Release/Acquire/AcqRel/SeqCst/Relaxed, omitting Consume)

authorities.rfcs: N/A (adopted from C++20 N4868 via library/core/src/sync/atomic.rs)
authorities.opsem: fcps.md:18,31 (atomic loads on read-only memory; rust-lang/rust#115577, #159503)

items.disagreements: stdlib (atomic.rs:25-58) normatively adopts C++20 (with RC11's psc SeqCst fence fix and access-based atomics), whereas MiniRust (spec/mem/concurrent.md) currently specifies only a sequential-consistency data-race detector without relaxed weak-memory read-from graphs, and OOTA (Out-of-Thin-Air) remains open in C++20.
items.rustc_deviations: On AArch64 with +rcpc (ARMv8.3-A), rustc/LLVM lowers Ordering::Acquire loads to LDAPR while lowering Ordering::SeqCst loads to LDAR; this is sound under C++20/RC11 but outside pre-ARMv8.3 IMM Coq proofs.

items.item: Unsynchronized overlapping atomic accesses of different sizes or alignments

authorities.opsem: rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines#345
authorities.minirust: spec/mem/concurrent.md:90-140 (rejects overlapping unsynchronized conflicting atomic accesses)

items.disagreements: Hardware models (x86-TSO and ARMv8 mixed-size) define byte-level coherence for overlapping mixed-size loads/stores, but stdlib (atomic.rs:42-55) and MiniRust make unsynchronized overlapping mixed-size atomic accesses UB (unless both are reads).
items.rustc_deviations: None; rustc lowers atomic intrinsics directly to LLVM atomic load/store/rmw instructions, which declare overlapping mixed-size unsynchronized accesses UB in LLVM LangRef.

items.item: Zero-sized accesses are no-ops; dynamic object size bounded by isize::MAX and no wrap-around

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:19,23 (ZST accesses/offsets are NOPs UCG#472; size_of_val with len 0 safe rust#126152)

items.disagreements: FLS (fls_oqhQ62mDLckN) states that creating an allocated object at base address null is UB, whereas Reference (r[undefined.dangling.def]), stdlib (NonNull::dangling), OpSem (UCG#472), and MiniRust allow 0-sized accesses at any non-null aligned address (and 0-sized raw pointer reads/writes even at null).
items.rustc_deviations: rustc and Miri agree that 0-sized reads/writes do not touch memory after alignment/validity checks.

items.item: Shared (&T freeze) and mutable (&mut T unique) aliasing principles and UnsafeCell<T> exception

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:24,34 (&UnsafeCell<T> to *mut T cast legal without .get() UCG#281; closures act like MaybeDangling rust#160745)

items.disagreements: Reference (r[undefined.alias]) explicitly notes that the exact aliasing model is not yet decided while fixing the boundary principles (function-call protectors on &T/&mut T except &T with UnsafeCell, Box<T> treated like &'static mut T). MiniRust adopts Tree Borrows; Miri supports both Stacked Borrows (default) and Tree Borrows (-Zmiri-tree-borrows).
items.rustc_deviations: rustc (compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/abi.rs:356-380) emits LLVM noalias + readonly on &T (when T: Freeze) and noalias on &mut T and Box<T> (when T: Unpin). Neither Stacked Borrows nor Tree Borrows is enforced for !Unpin mutable references in rustc today because of Pin<&mut !Unpin> self-referential generators (rust-lang/rust#63818).

items.item: Choice between Stacked Borrows and Tree Borrows (two-phase borrows, lazy Reserved->Active, offset range restriction)

authorities.reference: src/behavior-considered-undefined.md:25 (r[undefined.alias]: 'The exact aliasing rules are not determined yet')
authorities.opsem: fcps.md:24 (UCG#281 favors Tree Borrows over Stacked Borrows on &UnsafeCell<T> -> *mut T)

items.disagreements: Stacked Borrows (POPL 2020) eagerly activates &mut T on retag, restricts permissions to the slice subrange, and disables raw pointers derived from &UnsafeCell<T> rather than UnsafeCell::get(); Tree Borrows (PLDI 2025, MiniRust) lazily activates Reserved -> Active on first write, permits offset accesses within the allocation outside the initial reborrow size, and unifies two-phase borrows with ordinary mutable reborrows.
items.rustc_deviations: rustc emits MIR Retag statements (compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/builder/expr/stmt.rs) for Miri, and emits LLVM noalias/readonly/dereferenceable/writable/dead_on_unwind attributes in compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/abi.rs:350-490 that are sound under both SB and TB.

items.item: Pointer provenance requirement; Strict Provenance (addr, with_addr, without_provenance) and Exposed Provenance (expose_provenance, with_exposed_provenance)

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:21,29 (int-to-ptr transmutation questionable rust#122379; pointer byte order UCG#558)

items.disagreements: Transmuting an integer to a pointer (`transmute::<usize, *const T>(addr)`) vs `ptr::with_exposed_provenance(addr)` is marked questionable by OpSem (fcps.md:21, rust-lang/rust#122379): stdlib documents that integer-to-pointer transmute creates a pointer WITHOUT provenance (equivalent to without_provenance), whereas `as` cast (`addr as *const T`) equals `with_exposed_provenance(addr)`.
items.rustc_deviations: LLVM has not yet completed full byte-type / strict-provenance tracking for integer-to-pointer casts via memory (llvm/llvm-project#34548 / #35229), so LLVM optimizer bugs around `icmp eq` pointer-address replacement with mixed provenance remain a known upstream LLVM soundness hazard.

items.item: Pointer equality (ptr::eq / addr_eq / fn_addr_eq) and forbidden pointer-to-integer reinterpretation in const eval

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:29 (UCG#558)

items.disagreements: FLS does not specify CTFE provenance rules; Reference (r[undefined.validity.const-provenance]) and rustc CTFE (compiler/rustc_const_eval/src/interpret/validity.rs) strictly forbid reinterpreting pointer bytes with provenance as integer types during const evaluation.
items.rustc_deviations: At runtime, `ptr as usize` and transmuting a pointer to `usize` both succeed (the latter drops provenance without exposing it); at compile time (`const`), `ptr as usize` or transmuting a pointer with provenance to `usize` is rejected as a compile error / CTFE UB.

items.item: Immediate validity invariants for bool, char, !, scalars, enums, structs, tuples, arrays, NonNull/NonZero scalar ranges, and MaybeUninit
items.disagreements: FLS (fls_wacoqrtzvrwu) classifies `str` UTF-8 validity as a safety invariant, matching Reference (r[undefined.validity.str]: `str` validity is `[u8]`, i.e., initialized bytes, while UTF-8 is a library safety invariant).
items.rustc_deviations: rustc's `core::mem::uninitialized()` mitigation (ValidityRequirement::UninitMitigated0x01Fill in compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/layout.rs:207) fills memory with 0x01 rather than trapping on types that allow 0x01 unless `-Zstrict-init-checks` is enabled.

items.item: Union validity (all byte states valid) vs recursive reference pointee validity (&T pointing to invalid T)

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:25,26,27,35 (Validity of references does NOT depend on memory contents except uninhabited pointees UCG#414 & UCG#413; Unions are always valid UCG#438; enum discriminant transient change UCG#621)
authorities.minirust: spec/lang/values.md:110-180 (Unions allow arbitrary AbstractByte chunks; reference validity checks non-null, aligned, dereferenceable, not recursive memory content)

items.disagreements: Reference (r[undefined.validity.union], r[undefined.validity.reference-box]) still carries conservative text saying union validity is undecided and references must point to a valid value, whereas OpSem FCPs (UCG#438, UCG#414, UCG#413) and MiniRust have decided that (1) unions have trivial validity (any AbstractByte sequence is valid) and (2) reference validity does NOT depend on memory contents (except that `&!` / references to uninhabited types are uninhabited).
items.rustc_deviations: Miri and rustc CTFE (`compiler/rustc_const_eval/src/interpret/validity.rs`) enforce recursive reference pointee validity by default (`-Zmiri-validate-recursive` adjustments), while `rustc` LLVM codegen emits `dereferenceable(N) noundef align(A)` on references without reading pointee fields on function entry.

items.item: Type layout guarantees across repr(Rust), repr(C), repr(transparent), repr(Int), repr(C, Int), repr(packed(N)), repr(align(N)), and repr(simd)

authorities.rfcs: text/1358-repr-align.md; text/1399-repr-pack.md; text/1758-repr-transparent.md; text/2195-really-tagged-unions.md; text/2645-transparent-unions.md; text/3308-offset_of.md
authorities.opsem: fcps.md:8,13,14 (MSVC x86-32 8-align stack bug rust#112480; layout cannot change at runtime UCG#97; size == stride in arrays UCG#176)

items.disagreements: repr(Rust) field order, padding, and niche placement are explicitly unspecified (r[layout.repr.rust.unspecified]) except for the Option-like null-pointer optimization on single-non-zero-field structs/tuples (r[layout.option-null-ptr]) and ZST 0-size guarantees (r[layout.repr.rust.struct-zst]). Wide pointer (`*const [T]`, `*const dyn Trait`) field order (data pointer vs metadata) is explicitly unspecified (r[layout.pointer.unsized]).
items.rustc_deviations: 1) On i686-pc-windows-msvc, 8-byte aligned stack locals passed from C may only be 4-byte aligned (opsem fcps.md:8, rust-lang/rust#112480). 2) Zero-sized arrays/structs inside `#[repr(C)]` differ between C (GCC empty struct size 0 vs standard C11 forbidden) and C++ (`sizeof(Empty) == 1`); rustc gives `#[repr(C)] struct Empty;` size 0 and align 1 (r[layout.repr.c.struct.empty]). 3) 128-bit integers (`i128`/`u128`) had their alignment raised to 16 on x86_64 in LLVM 18 / Rust 1.77, matching C `_BitInt(128)` / `__int128` on SysV64 but differing on Windows MSVC where `i128` has align 16 while MSVC lacks native `__int128`.

items.item: Panic strategies (unwind vs abort), catch_unwind, and FFI unwinding across extern "C" vs extern "C-unwind"

authorities.opsem: rust-lang/rfcs#2945

items.disagreements: Reference (r[panic.unwind.ffi.undefined]) and RFC 2945 state that (1) a Rust panic unwinding out of a non-`-unwind` ABI (such as `extern "C"`) causes a process abort (via nounwind cleanup landingpad in rustc), whereas calling a foreign function that unwinds into Rust via a non-`-unwind` ABI, or calling a `"C-unwind"` fn through a transmuted `"C"` fn pointer that unwinds, is Undefined Behavior; and (2) catching a foreign exception (e.g., C++ `throw`) with `std::panic::catch_unwind` is Undefined Behavior (r[panic.unwind.ffi.catch-foreign]).
items.rustc_deviations: In `compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/layout.rs:1282` (`fn_can_unwind`), rustc attaches LLVM's `nounwind` attribute to `extern "C"` calls and injects an abort-on-unwind landing pad inside Rust-defined `extern "C"` functions.

items.item: IEEE 754-2008 roundTiesToEven arithmetic, non-deterministic NaN sign/payload rules (preferred, quieting, unchanged, target-extra), and CTFE vs runtime NaN divergence

authorities.opsem: rust-lang/rfcs#3514; rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines#237

items.disagreements: FLS describes floating-point types only as IEEE 754-2008 binary32/binary64 without specifying NaN payload propagation or SNaN passthrough; RFC 3514 and stdlib (`primitive_docs.rs:1244-1320`) normatively specify exact NaN bit-pattern sets and explicitly allow `SNAN * 1.0` to return an unquieted SNaN and CTFE NaN bits to differ from runtime NaN bits.
items.rustc_deviations: Known target non-conformances documented in RFC 3514 (text/3514-float-semantics.md:172-180): 1) 32-bit x86 (`i686` and `i586`) passes float return values in x87 registers (`fld`/`fstp`), which quietens SNaNs on return and violates bitwise-stability of passed-around floats (rust-lang/rust#115567); 2) `i586` without SSE2 uses 80-bit x87 intermediate precision (rust-lang/rust#114479); 3) legacy MIPS uses inverted SNaN/QNaN quiet bits (llvm/llvm-project#60796); 4) 32-bit ARM NEON flushes subnormals to zero.

items.item: asm!, naked_asm!, and global_asm! register clobbers, options (pure, nomem, readonly, preserves_flags, noreturn, nostack, may_unwind), and ABI invariants

authorities.fls: src/inline-assembly.rst:1-1779 (fls_zEtLZ5KjQcHS, fls_wydu9yft7a3r, fls_wh0wasawjj5s, fls_s0ivlbjefh1u); src/attributes.rst:872-880 (fls_0tYMAQY1V55p, fls_wGbJrz4OpKKb)
authorities.opsem: rust-lang/rfcs#2873, #2972

items.disagreements: Reference (r[asm.*]) and FLS (src/inline-assembly.rst) are closely aligned on stable architectures (`x86`, `x86_64`, `arm`, `aarch64`, `riscv32`, `riscv64`, `loongarch32`, `loongarch64`, `s390x`, `arm64ec`), requiring non-output registers, stack pointer, x86 DF=0, x87 stack empty, and FP control bits to be restored on exit.
items.rustc_deviations: Inline assembly is not supported in Miri or CTFE; LLVM's integrated assembler stateful directives (`.section`, `.pushsection`) must be restored before the end of the assembly block (r[asm.directives.stateful]).

items.item: Extern ABI strings ("Rust", "C", "C-unwind", "system", "system-unwind", "efiapi", "cdecl", "stdcall", "fastcall", "thiscall", "vectorcall", "win64", "sysv64", "aapcs", "custom") and call-site ABI matching
items.disagreements: `extern "Rust"` ABI is explicitly unspecified across compiler versions and flags (`compiler/rustc_abi/src/extern_abi.rs:281-290`), whereas `extern "C"` and platform-specific strings (`"sysv64"`, `"win64"`, `"aapcs"`, `"efiapi"`) must match the target's C psABI for FFI-compatible types (`#[repr(C)]`, `#[repr(transparent)]`, primitives, thin pointers, `Option<extern "C" fn(...)>`).
items.rustc_deviations: 1) Calling an `extern "C"` function via an `extern "C-unwind"` fn pointer (or vice versa) is permitted by UCG (`reference/src/layout/function-pointers.md`) ONLY as long as no unwind actually crosses the call, because their register/stack calling conventions are identical. 2) `i128`/`u128` in `extern "C"` was historically warned against by `improper_ctypes_definitions` until LLVM 18 aligned x86_64 `__int128` to 16 bytes (still differs on Windows MSVC where C has no native 128-bit integer). 3) Empty `#[repr(C)] struct S;` has size 0 in Rust vs size 1 in C++, causing ABI offset mismatch if passed by value to C++.

items.item: #[target_feature(enable = "...")] safety requirement, safe calls between matching target_feature fns, and #[instruction_set]

authorities.opsem: rust-lang/rfcs#2045, #2396

items.disagreements: Reference (r[attributes.codegen.target_feature]) and FLS (fls_xx51fjkbgg5g) agree that executing a function with an enabled target feature unsupported by the runtime CPU is UB, and that a safe function with `#[target_feature]` can be called safely from another function enabling a superset of those features (RFC 2396).
items.rustc_deviations: Passing SIMD vectors by value across a boundary where the caller and callee have mismatched target features (e.g. caller compiled without `+avx` calling an `#[inline(never)]` or indirect function compiled with `+avx`) can cause LLVM ABI vector-register mismatches (`rust-lang/rust#116558`); rustc lints/blocks `#[target_feature]` on functions that are coerced to safe `fn` pointers.

items.item: core::intrinsics internal compiler contracts vs stable stdlib wrappers (core::ptr, core::mem, core::hint, core::sync::atomic)
items.disagreements: `core::intrinsics::*` is permanently unstable (`#![feature(core_intrinsics)]`), so FLS and Reference only state that violating intrinsic preconditions is UB (`r[undefined.intrinsic]`). However, standard library crates (`core`, `alloc`, `std`) and verified compilers must implement the exact semantics documented in `library/core/src/intrinsics/mod.rs` and lowered in `compiler/rustc_codegen_ssa/src/mir/intrinsic.rs`.
items.rustc_deviations: Several intrinsics (`exact_div`, `unchecked_shl`, `unchecked_shr`, `ctlz_nonzero`, `cttz_nonzero`, `assume`, `unreachable`, `copy_nonoverlapping`, `transmute`) are lowered directly to MIR statements/Rvalues (`UnOp`, `BinOp`, `NullaryOp`, `CastKind::Transmute`, `StatementKind::CopyNonOverlapping`) before codegen, whereas others (`arith_offset`, `volatile_load`, `atomic_*`, `fadd_fast`, `catch_unwind`, `vtable_size`) remain call terminators lowered by backend intrinsic codegen.

items.item: Crate linkage types (bin, lib, rlib, dylib, cdylib, staticlib, proc-macro) and unsafe symbol/section attributes (#[unsafe(no_mangle)], #[unsafe(export_name)], #[unsafe(link_section)], #[used])

authorities.reference: src/linkage.md:1-183 (r[link.*]); src/abi.md:10-192 (r[abi.used], r[abi.no_mangle], r[abi.link_section], r[abi.export_name]); src/items/external-blocks.md:246-476 (r[items.extern.attributes.link.*])
authorities.opsem: rust-lang/rust#120363 (Edition 2024 unsafe attributes)

items.disagreements: In Rust 2024 edition (`r[abi.no_mangle.edition2024]`, `r[abi.link_section.edition2024]`, `r[abi.export_name.edition2024]`), `no_mangle`, `link_section`, and `export_name` require `#[unsafe(...)]` because symbol collisions or placing mutable statics into read-only linker sections causes UB. Rust symbol mangling scheme (`legacy` vs `v0`, RFC 2603) is an implementation detail for `Rust` symbols (`rlib`/`dylib`), whereas `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` and `#[unsafe(export_name = "...")]` guarantee exact exported symbol names.
items.rustc_deviations: `#[used]` (`r[abi.used]`) guarantees the compiler keeps the static in the object file, but the platform linker may still GC the section unless `#[used(linker)]` (unstable) or linker `KEEP` scripts are used (`rust-lang/rust#47384`, `rust-lang/rust#90769`).

items.item: ptr::read_volatile, ptr::write_volatile, and unaligned/copy volatile intrinsics (MMIO side effects, non-atomicity, trap on non-AM memory)

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:19,28,32 (ZST accesses are NOPs even for volatile UCG#472; atomic volatile should exist UCG#615; volatile accesses to non-AM MMIO memory may trap rust#160564)

items.disagreements: stdlib (`library/core/src/ptr/mod.rs:2149-2315`) specifies that `read_volatile`/`write_volatile` follow C11 volatile semantics, are NOT atomic across threads on RAM (unsynchronized concurrent volatile access to standard memory is a data race), and perform a no-op when `size_of::<T>() == 0`. OpSem recently finalized two FCPs (`fcps.md:28,32`): volatile accesses to non-Abstract-Machine (MMIO) addresses are allowed to trap (`rust-lang/rust#160564`), and atomic volatile operations are planned (`UCG#615`).
items.rustc_deviations: Because `read_volatile::<T>` returns `T` by value, reading a compound struct or slice via `read_volatile` may be lowered by LLVM into multiple memory instructions or `memcpy` rather than a single hardware instruction; only power-of-two primitive integer/pointer types up to target word size are lowered to single load/store instructions in practice.

items.item: GlobalAlloc::{alloc, dealloc, realloc, alloc_zeroed}, Layout (size <= isize::MAX, power-of-two align), and Box<T> layout equivalence

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:30 (Allocations are allowed to grow in-place, but not shrink: rust-lang/rust#159729)

items.disagreements: 1) `GlobalAlloc::alloc` with a 0-sized `Layout` is Undefined Behavior (`library/alloc/src/alloc.rs:125-145`); callers (`Box::new`, `Vec`) must handle ZSTs without calling the global allocator (using `NonNull::dangling()`). 2) OpSem FCP (`fcps.md:30`, `rust-lang/rust#159729`) specifies that allocations in the Abstract Machine may grow in-place (preserving existing pointers), but may NOT shrink in-place without reallocation.
items.rustc_deviations: rustc optimizes away unused ` __rust_alloc` + `__rust_dealloc` pairs (allocator elision via LLVM `allockind` attributes in `compiler/rustc_codegen_llvm/src/allocator.rs`), which means side effects inside a custom `#[global_allocator]` may be elided if the allocation does not escape.

items.item: Compile-time constant evaluation (const / static / const fn), immutability of promoted temporaries, and implicit rvalue static promotion rules

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:29 (UCG#558)
authorities.minirust: not modeled separately from runtime evaluation

items.disagreements: Explicit `const { ... }` blocks (RFC 2920) and `const`/`static` initializers have guaranteed compile-time evaluation rules (`r[const-eval.*]`). By contrast, **implicit constant promotion** (`&expr` promoted to `&'static expr`, RFC 1414) has a conservative syntactic rule in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/promote_consts.rs` (no `Drop`, no `UnsafeCell` except behind certain constructors, no fallible operations like `/` or `%` or in-bounds indexing that could panic/overflow), and Reference (`r[destructors.scope.const-promotion]`) leaves the exact set of implicitly promoted expressions partially implementation-defined while guaranteeing that any promoted memory is immutable (`r[undefined.immutable]`).
items.rustc_deviations: A drop-in `rustc` replacement MUST replicate `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/promote_consts.rs` (`validate_candidate`) for implicit `&`-promotion, because user code relies on `&0` or `&None::<Cell<i32>>` typechecking with `'static` lifetime without an explicit `const { ... }` block.

items.item: Deterministic drop order for locals (reverse declaration), structs/tuples/arrays/enums (declaration order, forward slice order), function arguments, and Edition 2024 tail-expression temporary scopes

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:16,17,22 (`*` projection not UB until access reference#1387; `_` pattern does not read or bind rust#103208; redundant StorageDead/StorageLive legal rust#99160)

items.disagreements: Reference (`src/destructors.md:1-645`), FLS (`src/ownership-and-deconstruction.rst`), and RFC 1857 agree on deterministic drop order: local variables drop in reverse declaration order; struct, tuple, and enum variant fields drop in declaration order (first field first, NOT reverse!); array/slice elements drop from index `0` to `len - 1`; closure captures drop in an unspecified order (`r[destructors.operation]`). In Edition 2024 (`r[destructors.scope.temporary.edition2024]`), temporaries in block tail expressions drop *before* local bindings in that block (rather than at the end of the enclosing statement outside the block).
items.rustc_deviations: Closure capture drop order is unspecified by the Reference (`src/destructors.md:88`), and `rustc` orders closure fields according to capture analysis in `compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/upvar.rs`. Also, unwinding during a destructor while already unwinding triggers an immediate abort (`core::panicking::panic_in_cleanup` in `library/core/src/panicking.rs`).

items.item: repr(Rust) struct/enum field ordering, niche placement (outside Option-like null-pointer optimization), and wide pointer (*const [T], *const dyn Trait) data/metadata field order

authorities.opsem: fcps.md:13 (layout cannot change at runtime within one execution, UCG#97)

items.disagreements: All authorities agree that `repr(Rust)` field offsets, enum discriminant encoding (outside `repr(Int)` / `repr(C)` and guaranteed null-pointer optimization), and wide pointer field order are explicitly unspecified across compiler versions and alternative compilers, provided layout is deterministic within a single compilation/execution (UCG#97).
items.rustc_deviations: A verified compiler does NOT need to match `rustc`'s field-reordering heuristic (`compiler/rustc_abi/src/layout.rs`) unless linking `rlib` crates compiled by `rustc` into the same binary; for standalone or source-recompiled crates, any deterministic layout satisfying alignment and size<=isize::MAX is compliant.

items.item: Calling convention of extern "Rust" / extern "rust-call" / extern "rust-cold" and drop order of closure captured variables

authorities.rfcs: text/1857-stabilize-drop-order.md (explicitly leaves closure capture drop order unspecified)
authorities.opsem: N/A

items.disagreements: None; Reference, FLS, and RFC 1857 explicitly leave `extern "Rust"` calling convention and closure capture drop order unspecified.
items.rustc_deviations: In `compiler/rustc_abi/src/extern_abi.rs:281-290`, `ExternAbi::is_rustic_abi` documents that `Rust`, `RustCall`, `RustCold`, `RustPreserveNone`, and `RustTail` are unstable across compiler versions.
